title: Full Recovery
concept: A six-step way to rebuild after a fight you keep having, or a genuine dent in trust — a real new agreement and a set time to prove it, not just a nicer evening.
whenToUse: When the same fight keeps coming back, or there’s a dent in trust you can both point to, and it’s too big for a normal Weekly Reset. Use it only when you’ve both agreed to sit down for it: never mid-fight, and not instead of a smaller repair.
steps: Warm up first — soften the mood before anything else. Don’t skip this.
Say what happened — each of you gives your side, and nobody interrupts.

Acknowledge the impact — do it before either of you explains. If one of you caused the breach (infidelity, lying, a broken agreement), only that partner acknowledges impact; the hurt partner is never asked to confess in return. If it’s drift rather than a breach, say so. Drift is nobody’s fault, but you can each name your part.
Explain, if asked — and only once the other person has really taken in the impact.
Ask for one change — name it, and agree a date for it.
Say it out loud, only if it’s true for both of you — “We made it through this. We’re still here.”

phrases.text: I want a Full Recovery conversation. Can we book it for when we’re both calm?
The agreement I’m asking for is ___, visible by ___.
We made it through this. We’re still here. (only if it’s true for both of you)

working: They book it for Saturday at 4pm, with phones in another room. They warm up, both say what happened, and A, who broke the agreement, acknowledges the impact before explaining. They agree one proof item for 14 days, checked weekly. Both mean it when they say they made it through.
notWorking: B brings it up at midnight, mid-fight, when they’re both too wound up to warm up. It becomes one more injury, and the real conversation now starts from further back.
activity: Set aside 60–90 calm minutes. Bring one issue only. Write down the agreement and the check-in date before you leave the room.
warn: Not mid-fight. Book it together, when you’re both calm, and never spring it on each other.
note: Deciding not to rebuild, or to end the relationship, is a valid outcome of this protocol, not a failure of it.
